title: Navigation Engine Task Response
description: Structured result returned by the generic navigation engine after a run completes (successfully, blocked, failed, or limit-exhausted). Raw website-derived evidence (captures) is kept separate from engine-generated classifications/reasoning (engineAssessment), per design requirement #8.

schemaVersion.description: Bumped from "1.39.0" to "1.40.0" for the radio-group classification fix (2026-10-07, follow-up to the evidence-first redesign below): resolveConsentGroups previously applied one uniform negative-option/opt-out resolution to every discovered radio group, which is only correct for marketing/privacy-consent questions -- a journey-intent question (quote vs. test drive vs. contact vs. brochure) or a customer/business-qualification question (private vs. business/self-employed/company) expressed as the same Oui/Non-shaped radio markup was silently resolved the same opt-out/last-option way, which is wrong for both. $defs referenced by formConsentDiagnostics.consentGroupDiagnostics (see src/forms/radioGroupClassifier.ts) now classify each group into marketing_consent/journey_intent/customer_qualification/ambiguous before resolving: marketing_consent keeps the original opt-out resolution; journey_intent is matched against the task's own existing workflow journey context (objective/active-milestone-texts/previous-CTA label) via generic multilingual semantic matching, never defaulted; customer_qualification always resolves to the private-customer option (a fixed automation policy, independent of any workflow field, and no new self-employed/company workflow input was added); ambiguous groups, and any confidently-classified group with no confidently-matching option, are left unresolved rather than guessed, feeding the pre-existing unresolvedRequiredConsentGroups/preSubmitReadinessFailures gate exactly as an unresolved group already did. consentGroupDiagnostics[] gains two new required fields (classification, classificationEvidence) and two new optional fields (selectionReason, present when resolved; unresolvedReason, present when not). This is additive to the schema shape; the one behavioural change is that a required journey-intent or customer-qualification group that previously always resolved (via the old uniform opt-out/last-option default) may now report unresolved and block submit when the new, more specific resolution rule cannot confidently apply -- the correctness fix this PR exists for. Bumped from "1.38.0" to "1.39.0" for the evidence-first dealer-resolver/consent-group/pre-submit-readiness redesign (2026-10-06, same Peugeot FR thread, following a manual live reproduction after the 1.38.0 fix still failed end-to-end): three further gaps confirmed from the live page. (1) formDiscoveryDiagnostics.dealerSearchWidgetDetected and the dealer_search upgrade were a single form-wide flag, so a form with two postcode-purpose fields (a plain customer-address postcode and a separate dealer-locator postcode/city sharing identical label vocabulary, e.g. both labelled similarly to "Postcode"/"Code postal") could only ever route BOTH or NEITHER through dealer_search; detection is now per-field, via structural adjacency (the nearest-preceding-sibling lookup control, same wrapper/fieldset relationship) to a lookup control, independent of the field's own label and independent of any other field's. (2) the lookup-trigger vocabulary lacked "select"/"choose" and their per-language equivalents (the live trigger read "Sélectionnez un Point de Vente", "Select a Point of Sale") and the prior design required an accessible result container to already exist in the DOM before the trigger was ever clicked, which is circular on any site (confirmed on this one) where the result container is only created after the click -- fill_form now detects the widget from pre-click-available structure alone (the field plus its adjacent control) and resolves the outcome generically afterwards: dealer_selected (a selectable result committed, verified by its own checked/aria-checked/aria-selected state, with a bounded two-stage retry for a location-suggestion list that itself never commits before the real dealer list replaces it), auto_populated (no selectable result ever appeared, but the lookup's own scoped text materially changed), or unresolved. (3) a consent question is very often expressed as Oui/Non-style radio groups whose own option labels carry no matchable keyword at all (the question text lives in a separate paragraph/legend) -- the per-field label-keyword matcher could never identify these, and an individual unmapped required radio previously fell through to a needs_claude call per option; actionResult gains a new formConsentDiagnostics object (always present whenever a submit was attempted or the readiness gate ran) reporting generic radio-group discovery (grouped by the shared HTML name attribute, question text found via fieldset/legend, aria-labelledby, or a bounded nearest-text walk), deterministic resolution (the same negative-option vocabulary an unmapped Yes/No dropdown already uses), and rescanning for conditional groups a selection reveals, bounded. A fourth, cross-cutting change: Submit is now gated by a new generic pre-submit readiness check (every required text/select field resolved, the dealer dependency -- if any -- verified, every currently-visible required consent group resolved) that must pass before Submit is ever clicked; a still-unresolved dealer dependency is now retried (bounded) BEFORE the first submit attempt rather than submitted anyway and retried afterward, per the explicit requirement that the engine never submit while a dealer-selection step exists but is unverified. formDealerSearchDiagnostics is restructured (still always present with explicit false/empty defaults) to: customerPostcodeFieldDetected, dealerLookupFieldDetected, dealerLookupFieldEvidence, dealerLookupControlDetected, dealerLookupControlEvidence, dealerLookupTriggered (was postcodeSearchTriggered), dealerLookupOutcome (new enum), locationSuggestionsDetected (new), locationSuggestionSelected (new), dealerResultsDetected, dealerAutoPopulated (new), dealerSelected, dealerValueVerified (was dealerSelectionVerified), dealerVerificationEvidence (new), dealerLookupFailureReason (new, optional) -- dealerResultsDetectedOutsideForm is removed (no longer meaningful once a result container existing beforehand is no longer a precondition). formPostSubmitDiagnostics gains preSubmitReadinessPassed, preSubmitReadinessFailures, submitAttempted (all required, always present). This is a behavioural redesign of the dealer-lookup and consent-handling flows, not a purely additive change -- a run that previously submitted with an unverified dealer dependency and let the site's own validation reject it now never clicks Submit at all in that case, reporting formFillOutcome "form_validation_failed" with submitAttempted: false instead. Bumped from "1.37.0" to "1.38.0" for the live Peugeot FR dealer-search-detection fix (2026-10-05, same thread as the 1.35.0-1.37.0 bumps: PR #78's own dealer_search flow never activated on the live site because the postcode field's own label text (e.g. "Code postal") carries no dealer-specific vocabulary, so matchLeadFormField matched the generic "postcode" purpose before ever reaching "dealerSearch", which can only ever match on label/name/placeholder/autocomplete text): fill_form now also detects a dealer-locator widget structurally -- a search-trigger control plus an accessible selectable-result container already present on the form (see src/forms/fillPlan.ts's hasDealerSearchWidget) -- and upgrades a field that would otherwise match generic "postcode" to the dealer_search decision when one is detected, independent of the field's own label wording. Separately, formDealerSearchDiagnostics was previously omitted entirely from the response whenever no field ever reached the dealer_search decision, making "the flow never activated" indistinguishable from "it activated and every step came back false"; it is now always present (with explicit false defaults) whenever a submit was attempted. formDiscoveryDiagnostics gains the new required dealerSearchWidgetDetected boolean (the same structural signal, independent of outcome), and formDealerSearchDiagnostics gains dealerResultsDetectedOutsideForm (diagnostic only, never used to select or click -- lets a future run tell a scoping gap, results rendering outside the <form> boundary the search is scoped to, apart from no results existing at all). All changes are additive except the postcode/dealerSearch decision upgrade itself, which only ever affects a field that would otherwise have gone through the dead-end fill_text path on a form that structurally has a dealer widget. Bumped from "1.36.0" to "1.37.0" for a fill_form dealer-search/post-submit-validation fix (2026-10-05, same Peugeot FR thread as the 1.35.0 and 1.36.0 bumps): the dealer_search decision only ever filled the postcode and pressed Enter -- it never waited for dealer results, selected one, or verified the widget actually committed that selection, so a site requiring a committed dealer before accepting the lead form kept cancelling submit even though every required field the engine could see was filled. Separately, post-submit validation (findInvalidFieldIds) was never re-run against a freshly re-tagged form, so a field a dynamic widget only revealed after the submit attempt (e.g. a hidden "selected dealer id" the widget writes once a selection is committed) was invisible to it -- formValidationMissingFields could report empty even though the site's own validation cancelled the submit. dealer_search now runs a generic postcode -> trigger search -> wait for results -> select the first result -> verify commitment flow (accessible role="radio"/"option" or radio-input results only, never a brand-specific selector), and every post-submit check re-tags the form first. Retries (still bounded at 2) are only attempted when a real corrective action is available -- an unverified dealer selection, or a set of invalid fields that differs from the previous attempt's -- rather than burning the budget repeating an attempt with no new evidence. New ActionResult.formDealerSearchDiagnostics (postcodeSearchTriggered, dealerResultsDetected, dealerSelected, dealerSelectionVerified) and formPostSubmitDiagnostics (submitCanceled, invalidFieldIds, nativeValidationMessages, postSubmitValidationMessages, retryDecision). All changes are additive except the dealer_search behavior and the post-submit re-tag themselves. Bumped from "1.35.0" to "1.36.0" for a fill_form field-discovery fix (2026-10-05, same Peugeot FR thread as the 1.35.0 bump): required-field detection only ever checked the HTML `required` attribute/`aria-required`, so a field a site marks required only with a visible marker (e.g. a bare "*" near its label, with no such attribute) was wrongly treated as optional and skipped -- and because the submit guard only tripped when at least one field had been *detected* as required, a run that detected zero required fields (due to this gap) still clicked Submit, which the site's own validation then cancelled. tagAndReadFields now also recognizes a visible "*" marker near a field's own label (any sibling of the label/field whose own text is exactly "*", or a label ending in "*") as required, with a bounded sibling/ancestor-walk label-linkage fallback for a control whose id doesn't resolve to any label's `for` (custom-widget-generated ids) and that isn't wrapped in a <label> either. A field whose current value only echoes its own label/placeholder text is no longer treated as "prefilled". The submit guard now also stops (`form_discovery_failed`) whenever the selected form's fieldActionabilityScore is 0 or nothing was actually filled, independent of whether any field was detected as required -- closing the exact gap that let the Peugeot FR run submit anyway. actionResult.formDiscoveryDiagnostics gains fieldDiagnostics (per-field label, control type, visibility, requiredEvidence, valueState, matched purpose, fill-plan decision, and whether it was filled), now required within formDiscoveryDiagnostics (itself still optional). All changes are additive except the stricter required-detection/prefilled logic and the broadened submit guard themselves. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.35.0". Bumped from "1.34.0" to "1.35.0" for the Lead-form filling journey-relevance form-selection fix (2026-10-05, same Peugeot FR thread as the 1.34.0 bump: scoring forms purely by actionable-field count is not sufficient -- a newsletter/search/utility form with more fields can outscore the correct, visually prominent request-a-quote form the engine's previous click/objective actually led to): fill_form's multi-form selection now scores every candidate on three independent signals (src/forms/formRelevance.ts) -- journey relevance (the form's own heading/submit-button/attribute text against the objective, the currently-unsatisfied required milestones' descriptions, and the previous step's clicked-CTA accessible name, plus a generic request-a-quote/offer/test-drive/contact/dealer-enquiry-vs-newsletter/search/login purpose signal), visibility/prominence (visible, main-content area rather than header/footer/nav chrome, a reasonably large area, a nearby heading, a visible submit control), and field actionability (supporting evidence only, 15% of the weight). actionResult.formDiscoveryDiagnostics gains journeyRelevanceScore, visibilityProminenceScore, fieldActionabilityScore, totalFormScore, selectedFormReason, rejectedFormsAndReasons (all now required within formDiscoveryDiagnostics, which remains itself optional). formFillOutcome's "form_discovery_failed" now also covers a selection below a defined confidence threshold, or an ambiguous top-two tie with no independently-verified tiebreak (an optional, bounded, evidence-cited Claude fallback resolver may break such a tie; its absence -- the default, same as the existing unmappedFieldResolver -- means the ambiguous band fails closed rather than ever guessing). All changes are additive except the new confidence-threshold/ambiguity submit guard itself. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.34.0". Bumped from "1.33.0" to "1.34.0" for the Lead-form filling multi-form-discovery/mapping-failure fix (2026-10-05, production Peugeot FR run: the engine always filled page.locator('form').first() even when several <form> elements existed, found zero matching fields on the wrong one, then still clicked its submit control, producing formFillOutcome 'form_validation_failed' with formFieldsFilled: [] and formValidationMissingFields: [] -- no diagnosable signal at all): the engine now scores every <form> on the page by how many fields its fill plan can actually act on and fills the highest-scoring one instead of always the first in document order; fill_form never clicks submit when at least one required field was detected but zero fields (deterministic or Claude-resolved) were filled, reporting the new formFillOutcome enum value "form_discovery_failed" instead. actionResult gains formDiscoveryDiagnostics (new, see its own property description): formsOnPage, selectedFormIndex, fieldsDiscovered, requiredFieldsDetected, requiredFieldsFilled, unmappedRequiredFieldIds, skippedFieldReasons -- present whenever fill_form found at least one form, independent of outcome, so a discovery/mapping failure is diagnosable without reproducing the run. All changes are additive except the new submit-guard behaviour itself (a run that would previously have clicked submit on zero filled fields now reports form_discovery_failed instead of attempting submission) -- no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.33.0". Bumped from "1.32.0" to "1.33.0" for Lead-form filling Phase 1 (docs/architecture.md "Lead-form filling"): the new fill_form action (the only action able to write a value into a form field, gated by safety.allowFormSubmission AND safety.allowPersonalDataEntry both being explicitly true) reports its outcome on actionResult -- formFillOutcome ("submitted"/"form_validation_failed"/"blocked_captcha"), formFieldsFilled, formRetriesUsed, formSuccessDetection ("url_change"/"on_screen_message"), formValidationMissingFields, formMarketDetected, formLanguageDetected, formClaudeCallUsed -- all optional, present only on a fill_form action's result; its submit-click and confirmation analytics are captured as two separate, stepIndex-tagged entries in the existing captures.data_layer_evidence/ga4_network_events arrays, reusing the generic per-step analytics pipeline rather than adding a new captures shape. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.32.0". Bumped from "1.31.0" to "1.32.0" for the start-page analytics capture fix (2026-09-30, production gap: GA4/dataLayer evidence fired during the initial page load -- before the first action -- was captured into captures.ga4_network_events/data_layer_evidence with stepIndex 0 but never turned into an analyticsReportingRow, since every action's own evidence window only ever starts counting from the array length at the moment that action begins, and the START_PAGE row itself had no pageUrl/pageTitle unless a task happened to request an explicit page_visits capture on stepIndex 0): analyticsReportingRows now includes stepIndex 0 ANALYTICS_EVENT rows built from the same pre-first-action capture window (actionId "<taskId>:start"), classified page_view/virtual-page-change evidence as ASSOCIATED_RESULT and everything else as RAW_CAPTURE_IN_ACTION_WINDOW, via the same classification/eventId/dedup logic every other row already uses; the START_PAGE row's sourcePageUrl/destinationPageTitle are now always populated from the engine's own post-navigation state, independent of whether page_visits was requested. All changes are additive -- no existing row shape changed, and action 1 onward is unaffected since its own window still starts counting only from where the start window ended. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.31.0". Bumped from "1.30.0" to "1.31.0" for low-memory resource-routing coverage across the full popup/new-tab chain (2026-09-29, follow-up to PR #71's own listener-handoff fix -- see src/api/browserResourceRouting.ts and docs/architecture.md "Low-memory browser mode"): resource routing now attaches at the browser-context level rather than only to the originally-tracked page, so it covers the run's original page and every popup/new-tab Playwright creates in that same context (adopted, nested, rejected, or otherwise) from the instant each one is created, recursively. $defs/resourceRoutingDiagnostics gains a new required byPage array ($defs/resourceRoutingPageDiagnostics, new) breaking the existing byResourceType run-level totals down per page (role, contextId/surfaceId once adopted, registration/navigation/closure diagnostics, its own byResourceType). Present only when LOW_MEMORY_BROWSER_MODE is enabled, exactly as before; every other diagnostics field is unchanged. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.29.0". Bumped from "1.28.0" to "1.29.0" for the Journey Memory re-observation/reconstruction gap fix (2026-09-28, production incident run_fae0519a-ef71-46b9-a053-4ca82bb30000, a 2nd occurrence after PR #68's own goBack-timeout fix: decision_point_restore_failed still fired with reObservationAttempted/fallbackNavigationAttempted both absent, and recoverySegmentsBuilt was 0 despite forwardSegmentsBuilt: 4 -- see docs/journey-memory.md and src/core/branchReturnRecovery.ts): $defs/routeAttemptDiagnostic gains reObservationAttempted, reObservationOutcome, fallbackNavigationAttempted, fallbackNavigationUsed, checkpointMatched, reconstructionOutcome, finalLiveVerificationOutcome (all optional; diagnostics.recovery.version moved "1.1.0" -> "1.2.0" for these new fields) -- populated whenever the branch-return-hop restoration path now performs bounded live re-observation and, as a last resort, checkpoint reconstruction before decision_point_restore_failed can fire, closing PR #68's own explicitly-deferred reconstruction piece. $defs/journeyMemoryDiagnostics gains recoveryCandidatesBuilt, recoveryCandidatesRejected, recoveryRejectionReasons (version moved "1.1.0" -> "1.2.0"), so a run with a genuine restore-failure incident but zero recovery segments now always carries an explicit reason rather than a silent zero -- this also closes a second gap where any "ambiguity"-entered bounded-branch return (as opposed to only "milestone_recovery"-entered ones) never wrote a routeAttemptDiagnostic/alternativeCandidateDiagnostic entry at all. All changes are additive and optional -- no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its unconditional meaning changed. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.28.0". Bumped from "1.27.0" to "1.28.0" for the Journey Memory remediation pass (2026-09-28, production incident run_b3743f06-1667-443e-b9fa-e804aa5caecf, decision_point_restore_failed -- see docs/journey-memory.md): actionResult gains optional goBackOutcome/goBackDiagnostics (see actions/goBack.ts); $defs/journeyMemoryDiagnostics.version moved from "1.0.0" to "1.1.0" for new optional fields lookupAttempted, forwardSegmentsBuilt, recoverySegmentsBuilt, segmentsWriteAttempted, writeFailureReason, persistenceConfirmed, and required diagnosticsAttached; $defs/recoveryMemorySegment (internal to journey-memory records, not part of this wire response) gains segmentSource so recovery segments built from routeAttemptDiagnostics/alternativeCandidateDiagnostics (not only recoveryAttemptDiagnostics) can be distinguished. All changes are additive and optional except diagnosticsAttached (required, but only within the already-optional journeyMemoryDiagnostics object, itself present only when JOURNEY_MEMORY_ENABLED is set) -- no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its unconditional meaning changed. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.27.0". Bumped from "1.26.0" to "1.27.0" for Persistent Cross-Run Journey Memory (2026-09-25, see docs/journey-memory.md and src/core/journeyMemory): diagnostics.journeyMemory (new, see $defs/journeyMemoryDiagnostics) reports the opt-in (JOURNEY_MEMORY_ENABLED, unset by default) cross-run memory system's pre-run/recovery lookup durations, candidates considered/accepted/rejected, which historical record influenced which decision (with its tier and confidence), whether an extra bounded recovery-focused reasoning call fired and its token/latency numbers, and confidence-change audit trail. This is purely additive and inert unless explicitly enabled: every existing task/response is byte-for-byte unaffected, and diagnostics.journeyMemory is entirely absent when the feature is off (the default). Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.26.0". Bumped from "1.25.0" to "1.26.0" for the engine-owned analytics reporting contract (2026-09-23, see src/capture-modules/analyticsReportingRows.ts and docs/n8n-analytics-reporting-migration.md): a new required top-level analyticsReportingRows array ($defs/analyticsReportingRow) carries final, flattened, deterministically-ordered reporting rows (START_PAGE/CTA_CLICK/ANALYTICS_EVENT record types) built from captures.cta_clicks' own actionAnalytics -- the engine now finalises correlation, classification, canonicalisation (a stable, non-reversible eventId per distinct captured event, expanding a bundled dataLayer push into its own distinct logical events), and deduplication itself, so a downstream consumer (e.g. n8n) reads this array directly instead of reconstructing reporting rows from ctaClicks/evidence arrays. This is additive: every existing captures/diagnostics field is unchanged, and analyticsReportingRows is always present (an empty array when a run captured no reporting evidence, e.g. no cta_clicks module requested). Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.25.0". Bumped from "1.24.0" to "1.25.0" for a focused analytics-classifier correction (2026-09-23, a real Peugeot configurator run exposed four classifier defects downstream of the confirmed-event-safety fix below): (1) the CLICK EVENT rules recognised too narrow a field-name vocabulary (link_url/link_id/cta/...) and missed common cross-vendor click fields -- eventLabel/event_label and Google Tag Manager's own gtm.elementText/gtm.elementUrl auto-event variables are now also recognised as CTA label/destination evidence, and an event/category/action naming a generic interaction verb (click/select/submit/request/open/continue/configure/redirect) is now itself click evidence, so a real CTA click tag (e.g. a uaevent or gtm.linkClick record) is no longer left CORRELATION_UNRESOLVED merely for using a field name the classifier didn't yet know. (2) analyticsCaptureSummary gains primaryClickEventStatus (CAPTURED/WEBSITE_NO_OBSERVED_CLICK_TAG/CORRELATION_UNRESOLVED/ENGINE_CAPTURE_INCOMPLETE/CAPTURE_UNCERTAIN_CONSENT_STATE), primaryClickEvent, supportingEvidence, associatedEvents, and unresolvedCandidates (new $defs/classifiedEvidenceItem, factored out of the existing classifiedEvidence item shape): the dedicated-click-tag outcome for an action is now reported separately from its overall `status`, so an action whose page/virtual-state evidence was fully captured but which emitted no dedicated click tag of its own is WEBSITE_NO_OBSERVED_CLICK_TAG, never miscast as CORRELATION_UNRESOLVED; when several records describe the same physical click (a rich business event plus a generic GTM auto-event trigger), the richest is reported as primaryClickEvent and the rest as supportingEvidence, never two primaries, and genuinely conflicting candidates (incompatible destinations) leave primaryClickEventStatus CORRELATION_UNRESOLVED rather than an arbitrary pick. (3) PHYSICAL_PAGE_CHANGE previously fired for any event merely carrying a page_location/full_url-shaped field; a distinctly-named business event that only carries that field as ambient context (e.g. a search/session event) is now left OTHER_MEANINGFUL_EVENT instead, while an explicit page-load event (page_view/pageview) or an event with no name of its own still qualifies exactly as before. (4) classifiedEvidenceItem gains its own triggerSegment (the existing PHYSICAL_CLICK/POPUP_OR_NEW_TAB/FALLBACK_NAVIGATION/DESTINATION_SETTLEMENT/RECOVERY/BACKTRACK vocabulary), populated per item rather than left for a caller to infer downstream. All changes are additive to the schema shape and generic (no brand/vendor-specific event names or domains). Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.24.0". Bumped from "1.23.0" to "1.24.0" for the analytics-capture-evidence confirmed-event-safety fix (2026-09-23, a real-site CTA-click analytics-correlation investigation -- see CLAUDE.md and capture-modules/analyticsCaptureClassification.ts). This closes two compounding gaps: (1) the URL-evidence gate previously required exact resultingUrl/destinationUrl string equality to attribute a GA4 request or dataLayer push to a click at all, which silently dropped real evidence differing only by tracking parameters or representing the same physical page under a different virtual/analytics identity -- actionAnalytics.ctaElementDestinationUrl (new, the clicked element's own declared destination, e.g. href, prior to navigation) and, per GA4 request/dataLayer push, analyticsEventDestinationUrl/analyticsPageLocation/analyticsFullUrl/analyticsVirtualPageUrl/analyticsVirtualPageMetadata (new, see $defs/analyticsVirtualPageMetadata) now carry the raw fields the evidence itself emits, actionResult.browserResultingUrl records the browser's own post-action URL independent of any evidence, and $defs/urlRelationship (EXACT_MATCH/TRACKING_PARAMETERS_ONLY_DIFFERENCE/SAME_PHYSICAL_PAGE/DIFFERENT_ANALYTICS_VIRTUAL_STATE/DIFFERENT_DESTINATION/UNAVAILABLE) plus a new triggerSegment (PHYSICAL_CLICK/POPUP_OR_NEW_TAB/FALLBACK_NAVIGATION/DESTINATION_SETTLEMENT/RECOVERY/BACKTRACK) replace exact-equality as the diagnostic, non-gating description of how evidence relates to the action. (2) a capture-window-ownership loophole meant any event merely observed inside an action's capture window -- including one with no location/destination field at all, e.g. an unrelated business event -- was confirmed as the action's own CTA/destination tag by default; classifiedEvidence (new, required on $defs/analyticsCaptureSummary, see $defs/analyticsCaptureSummary.classifiedEvidence) now tags every GA4 request/dataLayer push observed in the window with the specific, positive-evidence category it earned (CLICK_EVENT/PHYSICAL_PAGE_CHANGE/VIRTUAL_PAGE_CHANGE/FORM_OR_CONFIGURATOR_STATE/OTHER_MEANINGFUL_EVENT/CORRELATION_UNRESOLVED, see classifyEvidenceItem), and only the first four ever populate confirmedGa4Events/confirmedDataLayerPushes or the primary analyticsEventDestinationUrl/analyticsPageLocation/etc. fields -- window/segment ownership is necessary but never sufficient on its own. Both changes are additive to the schema shape (new optional/required-within-analyticsCaptureSummary fields only; no existing field removed, renamed, or had its unconditional meaning changed) and this repo's own convention (see below) bumps this const for every contract change, additive or not -- so the previous session's deliberately deferred bump (from "1.22.0" to "1.23.0", noted below) is folded into this one along with its own fields. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.23.0". Bumped from "1.22.0" to "1.23.0" for the click-success/milestone-evidence corrective work (2026-09-21, BMW live-site investigation -- see CLAUDE.md): actionResult gains one new optional field, verifiedSuccessType ("same_tab_navigation"/"new_context_adopted"/"dialog"/"settled_panel"/"destination_fallback_verified"), present only on a click action's result and only when success is true via one of these fixed, directly-observed evidence classes -- see its own property description for the full list and rationale. This closes two compounding gaps a real BMW UK live-site run exposed: (1) actions/click.ts's intercepted-click recovery path previously reported success on the strength of the target's own covered/disappeared state alone, with no corroboration, before ever attempting the destinationUrl fallback; it now additionally requires the already-computed, settled dialog/panel signal to agree, or falls through to the existing fallback + bounded stale-target recovery instead. (2) core/loop.ts previously forwarded a click's own declared destination (LastActionEvidence) to the semantic milestone verifier regardless of whether the click actually succeeded; it now does so only when verifiedSuccessType is present. Both changes are additive/narrowing on evidence quality only -- no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its unconditional meaning changed, and actionResult.success's own value is unaffected by either fix (a click that only ever produced the weaker, uncorroborated evidence still reports success: true exactly as before; it simply no longer also counts as strong enough evidence to corroborate a milestone). Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.22.0". Bumped from "1.21.0" to "1.22.0" for the surface-relevance corrective work, PR 6 (diagnostics/n8n extraction wiring -- see CLAUDE.md and docs/architecture.md "Surface adoption"): actionResult gains four new optional fields -- relevanceScore (0-1) and relevanceTier ("adopt"/"reject"/"ambiguous"), present whenever PR 3's relevance gate actually ran for a click's popup/new-context candidate, on both an adopted and a relevance_rejected outcome; consentActionTaken (boolean), present when PR 4's consent-only-candidate handling actually clicked a classifier-identified consent control; and extendedAllowedDomain (string), present only when an adopted candidate's domain trust was actually extended under surfaceAdoptionDomainPolicy "extend_trust_from_landing". actionResult.adoptionRejectedReason's enum gains "relevance_rejected" (the candidate's page signals did not clear the relevance adopt bar; previously computed internally by PR 3/4/5 but never reported on this contract). $defs/surfaceAdoptionAttemptDiagnostic mirrors all four new fields plus the widened reason enum, so diagnostics.surfaceAdoption.attempts carries the same evidence per lifecycle event. All changes are additive and optional -- no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed, and every existing task (which never sets Safety.allowSurfaceAdoption) is byte-for-byte unaffected. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.21.0". Bumped from "1.20.0" to "1.21.0" for Phase 3 PR 4 (return-to-parent recovery -- see CLAUDE.md and docs/architecture.md "Return-to-parent recovery"): diagnostics.surfaceAdoption (new, see $defs/surfaceAdoptionDiagnostics) reports every adopted-surface lifecycle event this run -- adoption, rejection (already reported via actionResult since PR 3, now also mirrored here), a verified return to the parent surface (a go_back while off "main"), a return that could not verify the parent surface, or the site itself closing an adopted surface unexpectedly -- so a caller can audit the full adopt/return lifecycle from one place instead of only from captures.errors' free-text diagnostic entries. Present only when at least one such event occurred. Bumped from "1.19.0" to "1.20.0" for Phase 3 PR 3 (new-tab/popup adoption -- see CLAUDE.md and docs/architecture.md "Surface adoption"): actionResult.surfaceAdopted (new, boolean) reports whether a click's own popup/new-context event was kept open as the engine's new active surface (observation.activeSurface becomes {"kind": "adopted_context", "identity": <surfaceId>} from the next step on -- buildObservation/dispatchAction/evaluateSuccessCriteria all then run against that adopted Page, including milestone satisfaction, multi-step action sequences inside it, and a nested popup opened from within it) instead of being captured (existing capture-modules/popupCapture.ts behaviour, unchanged when Safety.allowSurfaceAdoption is unset) and closed; actionResult.adoptionRejectedReason (new, optional) names why adoption was considered but not used ("domain_rejected"/"budget_exhausted") when it was not. Both fields are additive and optional -- no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed, and every existing task (which never sets Safety.allowSurfaceAdoption) is byte-for-byte unaffected. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.19.0". Bumped from "1.18.0" to "1.19.0" for Phase 3 PR 2 (active surface tracking scaffolding -- see CLAUDE.md and docs/architecture.md "Active surface tracking"): observation.activeSurface (new, see $defs/observation) reports which browsing context an observation's url/title/interactiveElements actually describe ("main"/"adopted_context"/"in_document", plus a short identity for the non-"main" case) -- always {"kind": "main"} as of this PR, since no adoption path exists before PR 3; this PR only makes today's implicit "which page is this" explicit and adds the prerequisite per-surface state-scoping plumbing (RunState surface stack; lastBlockerTargetId/lastBlockerSignature/route memory/low-confidence-retry fingerprints all now keyed per surface, transparently reproducing prior behaviour while there is only ever one surface, "main"). All changes are additive and optional -- no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.18.0". Bumped from "1.17.0" to "1.18.0" for Phase 3 PR 1 (adaptive settling -- see CLAUDE.md and docs/architecture.md "Adaptive settling"): actionResult.settleDiagnostic (new, see $defs/settleDiagnostic) and steps[].settleDiagnostic (a mirror of the same value for the step's dispatched action) report each settle wait's actual elapsed time and outcome ("quiet_window": the page went quiet before the ceiling; "ceiling_reached": it never did). This generalizes the pre-existing PR 1C-a click-only DOM-mutation-aware settle into a shared mechanism used by every settle point in the engine (post-navigation, post-click, low-confidence re-observation, popup-adoption capture), with a wider, task-configurable ceiling (task-request.schema.json's new settling.maxSettleMs, default 3000ms, hard-capped at 10000ms) replacing several previously-fixed wait durations. All changes are additive and optional -- no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.17.0". Bumped from "1.16.0" to "1.17.0" for the corrective pass (complete-route-exploration lifecycle diagnostics, multilingual consent handling, element-identity fix -- see CLAUDE.md and docs/architecture.md §23): diagnostics.recovery.routeAttempts[] (new, see $defs/routeAttemptDiagnostic) reports one record per candidate-route lifecycle transition (candidate_selected/route_active/route_progressing/route_succeeded/route_blocked/anchor_restore_required/anchor_restored/candidate_exhausted) -- proving a candidate route was genuinely followed for however many downstream actions it took, and evaluated for progress at each one, rather than only dispatched once and checked immediately; diagnostics.recovery.version moved from "1.0.0" to "1.1.0" for this new required field. observation.pageLanguage (new, optional) reports the page's own declared language (<html lang>, normalised to its primary subtag), one of several signals the engine's now-multilingual consent classifier (English/French/German/Spanish/Italian/Dutch) combines. diagnostics.consent.surfaces[] gained three new optional fields: resolvedViaModelAssist (true when a surface's own wording matched none of the configured languages and a caller-supplied bounded, independently-verified model-assist resolver identified the accept-all control instead), languageAmbiguous, and pageLanguage. All changes are additive and optional -- no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.16.0". Bumped from "1.14.0" to "1.16.0" for PR 1D (truthful milestone evaluation -- see CLAUDE.md and docs/architecture.md §21): diagnostics.milestoneEvidence[] entries now carry a required evidenceTier ("observed"/"inferred"/"assumed") classifying how evidenceSource established the criterion, and score is now always populated (1.0 for an "observed" entry, the existing deterministic-overlap/verifier-confidence value for an "inferred" one) rather than present only for semantic_page_match; engineAssessment gains an optional evidenceTierSummary (observedCount/inferredCount/assumedCount) rollup, present whenever at least one criterion was satisfied. This is observability-only: no criterion that would have satisfied before this change is newly withheld, and none that would not have satisfied now does -- assumedCount is always 0, enforced by an invariant test, since nothing in this evaluator ever satisfies a criterion without either observed or inferred evidence. The one narrowing change is that milestoneEvidenceRecord.score, previously optional and populated only for semantic_page_match, is now required and always populated -- every existing consumer reading it only when present is unaffected. No other existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.14.0". Bumped from "1.13.0" to "1.14.0" for PR 1C-a (drawer/modal/half-window surface detection beyond role="dialog"/aria-modal, post-click surface awareness, and readiness-based post-click timing -- see CLAUDE.md and docs/architecture.md §19): actionResult.surfaceChangeDetected/surfaceChangeType report, for a non-navigating click, whether a bounded, DOM-mutation-aware post-click readiness wait (replacing the previous fixed 250ms settle delay on this path) found generic evidence -- a dialog/modal appearing or changing, or a large newly-appeared fixed/absolute/sticky panel co-occurring with several new controls -- that a new interactive surface likely appeared. This is a separate, broader, non-target-attributed heuristic from the existing clickSideEffectDetected, which alone continues to govern click-success/route-progress attribution unchanged; the new fields are purely informational context threaded into the next reasoning-layer decision (an internal ReasoningContext.recentActions field, not part of this wire schema). All changes are additive and optional -- no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.13.0". Bumped from "1.12.0" to "1.13.0" for the target-attributable click-success fix (see CLAUDE.md and docs/architecture.md "Overlay-click side effect detection"): actionResult.clickSideEffectDetected and actionResult.fallbackVerified now require evidence attributable to the clicked target specifically (its own aria-expanded/covered state changing, or it disappearing -- see detectTargetAttributableSideEffect), not merely that something changed anywhere on the page; a fallback whose only evidence is an unattributed whole-page mutation no longer counts. actionResult.fallbackVerificationReason (new, present whenever fallbackVerified is present) names the specific mechanism that produced that verdict. actionResult.success is no longer unconditionally true for a fallback that changed the URL: it is now false whenever fallbackVerified is false, with staleTarget: true, giving the reasoning layer a further bounded recovery chance instead of silently reporting unverified progress as successful. observation.interactiveElements[].ariaState may now include aria-expanded, the same standards-based signal used for target-attribution. All changes are additive to the schema shape; the one behavioural (non-additive) change is actionResult.success's classification criteria for an unverified fallback, described above -- no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning silently changed for any other case. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.12.0". All new fields are additive and optional -- no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed. Version of this task-response contract, e.g. "1.11.0". Bumped from "1.10.0" to "1.11.0" for the overlay-click-detection fix (see CLAUDE.md and docs/architecture.md "Modal-aware observation" / "Overlay-click side effect detection"): observation.activeDialog (see $defs/observation) reports a compact, generic identity (role + short accessible-name excerpt) for a visible dialog/modal surface (role="dialog", aria-modal="true", or a native <dialog>), when one is present in the main document; observation.interactiveElements[].nearestHeadingText surfaces the nearest enclosing heading's text, found via a bounded ancestor walk, so repeated-card/list-item controls that share an identical role+accessibleName (e.g. the same-labelled action button under several different listing cards) can be told apart for route-memory candidate identity; actionResult.clickSideEffectDetected and actionResult.fallbackVerified report, respectively, whether a click that looked intercepted/timed-out was instead recognised as having actually succeeded from generic post-click evidence, and whether a generic destinationUrl navigation fallback's resulting page state was verified as a meaningful change rather than assumed equivalent to a real click. All four fields are additive and optional -- no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed. taskId.description: Echoes the taskId from the originating task-request.

statusReason.description: Short human-readable explanation of why the run ended in this status (e.g. which safety constraint triggered a block).

steps.description: Ordered log of every navigate/observe/decide/act cycle executed during the run.

analyticsReportingRows.description: Engine-owned analytics reporting contract (see $defs/analyticsReportingRow and docs/n8n-analytics-reporting-migration.md): final, flattened, deterministically-ordered reporting rows -- the single source of truth for downstream (e.g. n8n) reporting. Always present; an empty array is valid when the run captured no reporting evidence.

target.description: Selector, element id, or URL the action applies to, when applicable.

params.description: Action-specific parameters (e.g. scroll distance, wait duration, navigate URL).

staleTarget.description: True only when a failed action's cause was mechanically classified as the target having gone stale (hidden, detached, covered/intercepted, timed out, or its owning frame becoming unavailable) between decision and dispatch -- never a genuinely wrong or unsafe decision. Drives the engine's bounded, non-fatal recovery for exactly this class of failure.

clickSideEffectDetected.description: True only when a bounded post-click check found generic evidence, attributable to the clicked target specifically (its own aria-expanded/covered state changing, or it disappearing), that this click produced a real interaction-state change -- including the case where the direct dispatch appeared to fail as intercepted/timed-out because the overlay it opened came to cover the trigger itself, so the click is reported as a success on that basis instead of falling through to the destinationUrl fallback. An unrelated element elsewhere on the page changing at the same moment no longer counts. Absent (never false) whenever no such evidence was found or no check applied.

fallbackVerified.description: Present only when a generic destinationUrl navigation fallback was actually used to recover an unactionable click. True means the fallback's resulting page state was verified as a genuine, meaningful change attributable to the clicked target (a different page path/origin, or target-attributable evidence of a new interactive surface) rather than assumed equivalent to a real click; false means the fallback only changed the URL (e.g. a same-document hash-only navigation) with no verified further evidence -- in which case `success` is also false; an unverified fallback is never reported as a successful action.

fallbackVerificationReason.description: Present whenever fallbackVerified is present, naming the specific mechanism that produced that verdict -- e.g. "path_changed", a target-attributable side-effect type, or "unverified_hash_or_query_only_change". Purely explanatory, never itself a gating condition.

openedNewContext.description: True only when this click produced a "popup" event (a target="_blank" anchor or a window.open() call from a click handler) -- regardless of whether that context was successfully instrumented. Absent (never false) whenever no such context was opened.

observedNewContext.description: Present only when openedNewContext is true. True when the opened context was actually adopted long enough to attach analytics capture to it before being closed; false when it closed, navigated away, or otherwise became unavailable before instrumentation could attach. Never asserts the context produced any particular evidence, only that it was observed at all.

surfaceChangeDetected.description: PR 1C-a (drawer/modal/half-window detection beyond role="dialog"/aria-modal): true only for a non-navigating click whose bounded post-click readiness wait found generic evidence, via a broader, non-target-attributed heuristic than clickSideEffectDetected, that a new interactive surface likely appeared -- a dialog/modal appearing or changing, or a large newly-appeared fixed/absolute/sticky panel co-occurring with several new controls (the shape of a drawer/side-panel/half-window that never uses role="dialog"/aria-modal). Deliberately separate from, and never a substitute for, clickSideEffectDetected, which alone still governs click-success/route-progress attribution. Purely informational context for the next decision. Absent (never false) whenever no such evidence was found.

surfaceChangeType.description: Present only when surfaceChangeDetected is true, naming which heuristic matched: "dialog_appeared", "dialog_changed", or "layer_panel_appeared". Purely explanatory, never itself a gating condition.

settleDiagnostic.description: Adaptive settling (Phase 3 PR 1, see docs/architecture.md 'Adaptive settling'): present whenever this action ran a settle wait against the tracked page at all -- every navigate, and every click that doesn't fail before dispatch. Absent for an action type that never settles (scroll, wait, go_back, capture, the stop_* actions) and for a click that opens a popup/new context (that context's own bounded capture window settles independently and is never reported here).

surfaceAdopted.description: Surface adoption (Phase 3 PR 3): true only when this click's own popup/new-context event (openedNewContext) was actually kept open as the engine's new active surface (observation.activeSurface becomes "adopted_context" from the next step on), rather than captured (see observedNewContext) and closed. Absent (never false) whenever no adoption applied, including every run that never sets Safety.allowSurfaceAdoption.

adoptionRejectedReason.description: Present only when Safety.allowSurfaceAdoption was true and this click's popup/new-context event was considered for adoption but not kept open: "domain_rejected" (the landing hostname was outside allowedDomains under the "require_allowed_domain" policy, or never resolved to a real document), "budget_exhausted" (Safety.maxAdoptedSurfacesPerRun was already reached), or "relevance_rejected" (surface-relevance corrective work, PR 6: the candidate's page signals, optionally after one bounded consent-only-candidate interaction, did not clear the relevance adopt bar -- see relevanceScore/relevanceTier). The context was still capture-only-instrumented-and-closed exactly as if adoption had never been attempted.

relevanceScore.description: Surface-relevance corrective work (PR 6): present whenever the relevance gate actually ran for this click's popup/new-context candidate (Safety.allowSurfaceAdoption true, a non-empty relevance objective text, adoption budget not already exhausted) -- on an adopted candidate and a relevance_rejected one alike, never only one. The final deterministic token-overlap score against RELEVANCE_ADOPT_THRESHOLD (0.35)/RELEVANCE_REJECT_THRESHOLD (0.08) -- both still initial, unvalidated calibration values pending live-site validation (PR 7), never to be read as production-proven. Reflects the reassessment after a consentActionTaken interaction when one occurred.

relevanceTier.description: Companion to relevanceScore, present under the exact same condition: the three-tier relevance classification. "ambiguous" appears here only when it was never resolved to a confident verdict; a resolved ambiguous candidate is reported as whichever of "adopt"/"reject" the resolution (and any following consent interaction) settled on.

consentActionTaken.description: Consent-only-candidate handling (PR 4, widened in PR 6 to every non-relevant tier): true only when this candidate's only visible content was a genuine, classifier-identified consent surface and the one bounded, policy-approved ("accept_optional") click against it actually succeeded, after which relevanceScore/relevanceTier reflect the reassessment of the revealed content. Absent (never false) whenever no such interaction was attempted, was attempted but failed, or no consent surface was detected.

extendedAllowedDomain.description: Surface adoption (Phase 3 PR 3, wired onto the wire in PR 6): present only when this candidate was actually adopted (surfaceAdopted true) under Safety.surfaceAdoptionDomainPolicy "extend_trust_from_landing" and its own landing hostname was outside the run's allowedDomains -- names that hostname, trusted only for this one adopted surface's own lifetime. Never widens the run's own allowedDomains; absent whenever the adopted candidate's hostname was already within allowedDomains, or the domain policy was "require_allowed_domain" (the default).

candidateSurfaceFingerprint.description: Popup fingerprinting and retry protection (surface-adoption corrective work, schemaVersion 1.30.0): a sanitized, generic identity (normalized hostname, a truncated path shape with no query string, and the triggering click's own stable identity) for this popup/new-context candidate -- see core/surfaceFingerprint.ts. Present whenever the relevance gate ran and the triggering click's identity was resolvable. Never includes a query parameter, cookie, token, or personal data.

fingerprintPreviouslySeen.description: Popup fingerprinting and retry protection: true when this exact candidateSurfaceFingerprint already had a recorded relevance outcome from an earlier encounter this same run (e.g. the reasoning layer re-selected the same CTA after backtracking). Present under the same condition as candidateSurfaceFingerprint.

popupReconsiderationReason.description: Popup fingerprinting and retry protection: present only when fingerprintPreviouslySeen is true. "cached_no_new_evidence" means the cached tier/score from the earlier encounter was reused verbatim, without re-running the relevance gate or making another Claude ambiguity call. "bounded_reconsideration" means this was the one-in-N repeat encounter where the candidate was deliberately rescored in full (see FINGERPRINT_RECONSIDERATION_INTERVAL, capture-modules/popupCapture.ts).

verifiedSuccessType.description: Click-success/milestone-evidence corrective work (2026-09-21, BMW live-site investigation): present only on a click action's result, and only when success is true on the strength of one of these fixed, directly-observed evidence classes -- strong enough for core/loop.ts to forward this click's own details (LastActionEvidence) to corroborate a semantic_page_match milestone. "same_tab_navigation": a real, allowedDomains-checked navigation of the tracked page. "new_context_adopted": the popup/new-context event was kept open as the engine's new active surface (already relevance-gated). "dialog": a standards-based dialog/modal signal (role="dialog", aria-modal="true", or a native <dialog>) appeared or changed. "settled_panel": after the same bounded settle wait used elsewhere, a large newly-appeared panel co-occurred with several new controls. "destination_fallback_verified": the generic destinationUrl navigation fallback was used and verified as a genuine, target-attributable change. Absent whenever success is false, or true only via weaker, uncorroborated evidence (a target becoming covered/disappearing/re-rendering, or an uneventful click with no further observable effect) -- success itself is unaffected by this narrower field.

goBackOutcome.description: go_back timeout/classification fix (production incident run_b3743f06-1667-443e-b9fa-e804aa5caecf, see actions/goBack.ts): present only on a go_back action's result. "restoration_verified" is never set by the executor itself -- only core/loop.ts ever assigns it, after live re-observation evidence confirms the destination; a changed URL alone never means "restoration_verified".

goBackDiagnostics.description: Sanitized diagnostics backing goBackOutcome -- URL identity only, never cookies/tokens/PII.

formFillOutcome.description: Lead-form filling (Phase 1, see docs/architecture.md 'Lead-form filling'): present only on a fill_form action's result. "submitted": the form was submitted and either a URL change or an on-screen confirmation was observed (see formSuccessDetection). "form_validation_failed": submission was retried up to the bound (see formRetriesUsed) and still reported missing/invalid required fields (see formValidationMissingFields). "blocked_captcha": a CAPTCHA was detected before submission; the engine never attempts to solve or bypass it. "form_discovery_failed": either (a) at least one visible required field was detected on the selected form but zero fields could be filled deterministically or via the Claude fallback, or (b) no candidate form reached the multi-form-selection confidence threshold, or an ambiguous tie between the top two candidates had no independently-verified tiebreak -- in every case the engine never clicked submit at all -- see formDiscoveryDiagnostics for why.

formFieldsFilled.description: Generic field keys (e.g. "firstName", "email", "mobilePhone", "postcode") this fill_form action actually wrote a value into. Never the raw value itself -- only which fixed test-data field was used, for auditability.

formRetriesUsed.description: Number of validation-triggered re-fill-and-resubmit cycles this fill_form action performed, bounded at 2.

formSuccessDetection.description: Present only when formFillOutcome is "submitted": which mechanism confirmed success -- a new/changed URL, or an on-screen confirmation dialog/text with no URL change.

formValidationMissingFields.description: Present only when formFillOutcome is "form_validation_failed": the generic field keys still reported missing/invalid after the retry bound was reached.

formMarketDetected.description: The market code (e.g. "FR", "DE") whose fixed postcode/phone test data this fill_form action used.

formLanguageDetected.description: The page language (e.g. "fr", "de") this fill_form action used to select the title value and localized option/keyword matching.

formClaudeCallUsed.description: True only when the one optional, bounded Claude call for unmapped required fields (see CLAUDE.md 'minimise Claude API calls') was actually made for this form. Absent (never false) when every required field was resolved deterministically.

formDiscoveryDiagnostics.description: Present whenever fill_form found at least one <form> on the page -- generic discovery/mapping diagnostics so a discovery/mapping failure (e.g. formFillOutcome 'form_discovery_failed', or zero formFieldsFilled on any outcome) is diagnosable without reproducing the run. Never brand- or site-specific: field identities are the engine's own generic field-index ids, never raw page text/values.

formsOnPage.description: How many <form> elements were on the page; when more than one, the engine scores every candidate and fills the one with the most actionable fields rather than always the first in document order.

selectedFormIndex.description: Document-order index of the <form> the engine chose to fill.

fieldsDiscovered.description: Total input/select/textarea elements found inside the selected form.

requiredFieldsDetected.description: Of those, how many were visible and required.

requiredFieldsFilled.description: Of the required fields, how many the engine actually wrote a value into (deterministically or via the Claude fallback) before submit was attempted.

dealerSearchWidgetDetected.description: Structural, generic detection of a dealer-locator widget on the selected form: a search-trigger control (a nearby search/go/find/ok-labelled button) plus an accessible selectable-result container (role="radio"/"option" or a radio input), independent of whether any field's own label mentions 'dealer' or an equivalent -- see src/forms/fillPlan.ts's hasDealerSearchWidget. A dealer-locator's own postcode field is very often labelled identically to a plain postcode field, so this cannot be decided from label text alone.

unmappedRequiredFieldIds.description: Generic field-index ids of required fields the engine could not map to any known field (no deterministic keyword match and no Claude fallback resolution, or a select control with no usable options).

skippedFieldReasons.description: One entry per field the fill plan decided to skip, with the generic reason (mirrors src/forms/fillPlan.ts's FillDecision 'skip' reasons).

journeyRelevanceScore.description: How well the selected form's own text (nearby heading, submit-button text, form attributes, page title/headings) matches the objective/active-milestone/previous-clicked-CTA anchors, plus a generic request-a-quote/offer/test-drive/contact/dealer-enquiry-vs-newsletter/search/login purpose signal -- see src/forms/formRelevance.ts's scoreJourneyRelevance.

visibilityProminenceScore.description: Visual prominence of the selected form: visible, in the main content area rather than header/footer/nav chrome, a reasonably large visible area, a nearby heading, a visible submit control -- see src/forms/formRelevance.ts's scoreVisibilityProminence.

fieldActionabilityScore.description: Supporting evidence only, never the primary selection signal: the fraction of the selected form's own fields the deterministic fill plan could actually act on.

totalFormScore.description: Weighted combination of journeyRelevanceScore, visibilityProminenceScore, and fieldActionabilityScore (journey relevance and visibility/prominence together carry 85% of the weight). Both form selection and the submit guard (formFillOutcome 'form_discovery_failed' below a defined confidence threshold) are decided from this.

selectedFormReason.description: Human-readable explanation of why the selected form was chosen -- its score breakdown, or, when no candidate reached the confidence threshold or an ambiguous tie between the top two candidates couldn't be verified, why none was safely selectable.

rejectedFormsAndReasons.description: Every candidate form other than the selected one, with its own total score and why it was not chosen.

requiredEvidence.description: Where `required` came from for this field: the HTML `required`/`aria-required` attribute, a visible marker (e.g. a bare "*") near the field with no such attribute, or neither.

valueState.description: 'placeholder_mimicry': the field's current value only echoes its own label/placeholder text (a site rendering its placeholder into the live value) -- never treated as real prefilled data.

matchedField.description: The generic lead-form field purpose this field was matched to (see src/forms/fieldKeywords.ts's LeadFormFieldKey), if any.

decision.description: The fill plan's decision kind for this field (see src/forms/fillPlan.ts's FillDecision).

fieldDiagnostics.description: Per-field evidence for the selected form -- label, control type, visibility, where `required` came from, current-value state, matched purpose (if any), the fill-plan decision, and whether it was actually filled. Lets a discovery/mapping failure be diagnosed field-by-field from the response alone, without reproducing the run.

formDealerSearchDiagnostics.description: Present (with explicit false/empty defaults) whenever a submit was attempted or the pre-submit readiness gate ran -- diagnostics for the generic postcode/city -> lookup -> (auto-populate | location-suggestion | selectable dealer list) -> verify flow a dealer_search decision drives. A form can have two postcode-purpose fields (a plain customer-address postcode and a separate dealer-locator postcode/city) sharing identical label vocabulary; detection is per-field (structural adjacency to a lookup control), never a form-wide flag. requiredFieldsFilled being non-zero is never, by itself, proof this dynamic widget's dependent selection is complete; dealerValueVerified is the only field that confirms it.

customerPostcodeFieldDetected.description: A plain (non-dealer) postcode-purpose field was also present on the chosen form, distinct from the dealer-lookup postcode/city field.

dealerLookupFieldDetected.description: A field was identified as serving the dealer-lookup purpose, by keyword match or by structural adjacency to a lookup control.

dealerLookupControlDetected.description: The dealer-lookup field had its own structurally-adjacent lookup control (not just a keyword match with no control found, which falls back to pressing Enter).

dealerLookupTriggered.description: True once the postcode/city was entered and the lookup was activated (the adjacent control, or Enter as a generic fallback).

dealerLookupOutcome.description: The resolver inspects the resulting state rather than assuming one fixed shape: 'auto_populated' (no selectable result ever appeared, but the lookup's own scoped text materially changed), 'dealer_selected' (a selectable result was clicked and its own state verified the commit), 'unresolved' (neither happened within the bound), 'not_applicable' (no dealer_search decision ever ran).

locationSuggestionsDetected.description: At least one accessible selectable candidate (role="radio"/"option" or a radio input) appeared after the lookup was triggered -- could be a location-geocoding suggestion or the final dealer list; the resolver tells them apart by whether a selection verifiably commits.

locationSuggestionSelected.description: True only for the two-stage case: the first selectable list never committed, a second list replaced it shortly after, and that second list's first result was selected instead.

dealerResultsDetected.description: True when at least one accessible dealer-result candidate appeared (an alias of locationSuggestionsDetected kept for this flow's final-selection step).

dealerAutoPopulated.description: True when the dealer value was treated as auto-populated (lookupOutcome 'auto_populated').

dealerSelected.description: True when a selectable result was clicked.

dealerValueVerified.description: True only when either the auto-populate text-change evidence was observed, or the selected result's own state (checked, aria-checked="true", or aria-selected="true") confirmed the widget's JS committed the selection. False means the dependency is not safely resolved -- the generic signal that retrying the lookup (bounded, before Submit is ever clicked) is worth attempting.

dealerLookupFailureReason.description: Present only when the lookup outcome is 'unresolved' -- why (e.g. a selectable result was found but never verifiably committed, or neither a selectable result nor a text change was observed within the bound).

formConsentDiagnostics.description: Present whenever a submit was attempted or the pre-submit readiness gate ran -- generic radio-group consent discovery/resolution diagnostics, always present even when zero consent groups exist on the form. A consent question is very often expressed as Oui/Non-style radios whose own option labels carry no matchable keyword at all, so this never goes through the per-field label-keyword matcher; groups are discovered by the shared HTML `name` attribute and a nearby question text (fieldset/legend, aria-labelledby, or bounded nearest-text walk), then resolved with the same deterministic negative-option vocabulary an unmapped Yes/No dropdown already uses, re-scanning for newly-revealed conditional groups until none remain or the bounded loop limit is reached.

classification.description: Three-way radio-group taxonomy result (see src/forms/radioGroupClassifier.ts). "ambiguous" is never resolved by this engine.

selectionReason.description: Present only when resolved: why this option was selected.

unresolvedReason.description: Present only when not resolved: why this group was left unresolved rather than guessed.

unresolvedRequiredConsentGroups.description: Visible groups with evidence of being required (the HTML required/aria-required attribute, or a visible marker near the question text) that never got a checked member -- the generic pre-submit readiness gate blocks Submit on these.

formPostSubmitDiagnostics.description: Present whenever a submit control was found and clicked, or the pre-submit readiness gate ran -- live validation evidence read immediately after each submit attempt (fields are re-tagged first, so a field a dynamic widget only reveals after the submit attempt, such as a dealer-selection widget's own hidden committed-selection field, is never invisible to it).

submitCanceled.description: True whenever, after any retries, the submit did not result in a URL change or an on-screen confirmation -- or whenever Submit was never clicked at all because the pre-submit readiness gate failed.

invalidFieldIds.description: Generic field-index ids still failing native constraint validation or carrying aria-invalid="true" after the last submit attempt.

nativeValidationMessages.description: Each invalid field's own native validationMessage, keyed by its generic field-index id.

postSubmitValidationMessages.description: Visible validation/error text found in the form (role="alert", aria-live, or a generic error/invalid-feedback class) after the last submit attempt.

retryDecision.description: Human-readable explanation of whether a retry was attempted and why (or why not) -- e.g. no corrective action identified, same fields still invalid with no new evidence, which corrective action (re-filling fields vs. re-running the dealer lookup) was taken, or that Submit was never attempted because the readiness gate failed.

preSubmitReadinessPassed.description: False only when the generic pre-submit readiness gate (required fields, dealer dependency, required consent groups) failed and Submit was never clicked at all.

preSubmitReadinessFailures.description: Each failed readiness condition, e.g. "unresolved_required_fields:3,7", "dealer_dependency_unresolved", "unresolved_required_consent_groups:marketingConsent". Empty when the gate passed.

submitAttempted.description: False only when the pre-submit readiness gate failed and Submit was never clicked.

settleDiagnostic.description: Adaptive settling (Phase 3 PR 1): the outcome of one bounded wait for the page to go quiet after an action or navigation. `elapsedMs` is always <= the effective ceiling used for that wait (task.settling.maxSettleMs when the task set one, else the engine default, itself always <= the hard 10000ms cap).

reason.description: "quiet_window": the page (DOM mutations and the interactive-element candidate count alike) was quiet for the configured window before the ceiling was reached -- the common, fast-page case. "ceiling_reached": the page never quieted and the wait was cut off at the ceiling, never longer.

estimatedCompletion.description: Engine's 0-1 estimate of progress toward success; a classification, not raw evidence.

observation.description: Compact structured summary of the page derived from visible and accessible elements. Never the raw HTML document.

interactiveElements.description: Condensed list of clickable/actionable elements available to the reasoning layer.

id.description: Stable reference the engine can resolve back to a Playwright locator.

destinationUrl.description: Destination URL of the element, when available (e.g. an anchor's href), surfaced to the reasoning layer so it can distinguish navigation targets without raw HTML.

disabled.description: True when the element carries a disabled attribute or aria-disabled="true".

ariaState.description: Generic ARIA selection/toggle-state attribute values present on this element (aria-selected/aria-checked/aria-pressed/aria-current), read verbatim from the page and never normalised into an engine-defined closed set.

covered.description: True when another element currently sits visually on top of this element's centre point (e.g. a modal, overlay, or banner), determined by the same elementFromPoint hit-test the engine uses to revalidate a click target immediately before dispatch. A covered element is still visible and still reported -- this only tells the reasoning layer it is not currently reachable by a click.

frameOrigin.description: Origin (scheme+host+port, never a full URL) of the same-origin child frame this element was found in -- present only for an element outside the main document. Absent for every main-document element, which remains the overwhelming common case.

nearestHeadingText.description: Short (<=80 char) text of the nearest enclosing heading (h1-h4), found via a bounded ancestor walk -- a cheap, markup-agnostic proxy for which repeated card/list-item this control is part of. Used to disambiguate route-memory candidate identity for controls that would otherwise share an identical role+accessibleName across multiple repeated cards. Absent when no heading was found within the bounded walk.

activeDialog.description: Present when a visible dialog/modal surface (role="dialog", aria-modal="true", or a native <dialog>) exists in the main document at the time of this observation. A compact, generic identity only -- never the dialog's full content, which is still carried element by element in interactiveElements as usual.

pageLanguage.description: The page's own declared language (<html lang>), normalised to its primary subtag only (e.g. "fr-FR" -> "fr") -- one signal among several the engine's consent classifier combines, never a translation and never used on its own to decide anything. Absent when the page declares no language.

activeSurface.description: Active surface tracking scaffolding (Phase 3 PR 2, see docs/architecture.md 'Active surface tracking'): which browsing context this observation's url/title/interactiveElements actually describe. Present on every observation once this field ships (absent only for a response built before Phase 3 PR 2). Always {"kind": "main"} as of PR 2 -- no PR before PR 3 wires an actual adoption path.

kind.description: "main": the engine's originally-tracked page. "adopted_context": a separate Page object (a popup/new tab) genuinely adopted as the active navigation context. "in_document": a same-document surface (a drawer/modal/side panel) the engine is treating as the active context.

identity.description: Short, generic identity for a non-"main" surface (e.g. its own url or title). Absent for "main".

notableText.description: Short list of salient visible text snippets (headings, prices, banners) surfaced to the reasoning layer without sending full page content.

progressIndicatorText.description: Generic, brand-agnostic progress-indicator text (e.g. "Step 2 of 4"), read from any element the page itself marks up as a progress/step indicator (role="progressbar", aria-valuenow, aria-current="step").

inaccessibleFrameOrigins.description: Bounded (capped small), deduplicated list of origins of same-origin-scan-eligible child frames the engine detected but could not evaluate script in at the time of this observation (removed mid-scan, or otherwise inaccessible). Never frame content, never a reason beyond the fact that it couldn't be read.

elementDiscoveryDiagnostics.description: Bounded, generic diagnostic evidence about the interactive-element scan itself, always computed alongside interactiveElements -- lets a caller distinguish a genuinely empty page from one whose controls were excluded (hidden/zero-size) or live inside a structure this scan cannot see (a non-zero shadowHostCount alongside an empty interactiveElements is the generic signature of that specific gap). Summed across the main document and every accessible child frame, matching how interactiveElements itself is a flat cross-frame list.

rawElementCount.description: Every node matched by the same interactive-element selector interactiveElements is built from, before any visibility filtering. rawElementCount > 0 with interactiveElements empty means candidates existed but were all excluded; rawElementCount === 0 means the selector matched nothing at scan time at all.

buttonLikeCount.description: Of rawElementCount, elements whose role or tag is "button".

linkLikeCount.description: Of rawElementCount, elements whose role or tag is "a"/"link".

otherRoleCount.description: Of rawElementCount, everything else the selector matches (tabs, options, radio/checkbox-style controls, submit/button inputs, etc.). buttonLikeCount + linkLikeCount + otherRoleCount always equals rawElementCount.

visibleElementCount.description: Elements that survived the visibility filter -- equals interactiveElements.length for this same scan.

excludedZeroSizeCount.description: Of the excluded elements, how many had zero width or height. Not mutually exclusive with the other excluded*Count fields -- a single element can match more than one reason -- so these need not sum to (rawElementCount - visibleElementCount).

excludedDisplayNoneCount.description: Of the excluded elements, how many had computed style display: none.

excludedVisibilityHiddenCount.description: Of the excluded elements, how many had computed style visibility: hidden.

shadowHostCount.description: Count of elements in the document with a non-null, *open* shadow root. A closed shadow root's presence is fundamentally undetectable from outside the component that created it, so a page using closed shadow DOM can still report shadowHostCount: 0 despite hosting undiscoverable controls.

decision.description: Constrained rationale text produced by the reasoning layer for choosing the selected action.

progress.description: Snapshot of success-criteria evaluation after this step.

safetyFlags.description: Any guardrails that were evaluated and triggered on this step (e.g. domain_blocked, loop_detected, repeated_action, form_submission_blocked, required_criteria_unsatisfied).

reObservationAttempted.description: True when this step's pre-dispatch revalidation found the originally-decided click target no longer actionable and asked the reasoning provider again against a freshly rebuilt observation before dispatching anything.

recoveryAttempts.description: How many additional decision/revalidation cycles this step's pre-dispatch recovery used before settling on the action it actually dispatched -- bounded by a small fixed constant.

settleDiagnostic.description: Mirrors actionResult.settleDiagnostic for this step's dispatched action -- see its own doc comment.

captures.description: Raw, website-derived evidence collected by capture modules, keyed by module name. Only modules the task requested are populated. This section must contain evidence as observed, not engine interpretation.

page_metadata.description: Generic per-page metadata (title, meta description, lang) as read from the document, with no engine interpretation.

finish_page_ctas.description: Visible calls-to-action found on the page at capture time (e.g. a journey's finish/success state). Generic element evidence only — no domain-specific classification.

text.description: Visible text of the CTA element as rendered on the page.

url.description: Destination URL of the CTA, when available (e.g. an anchor's href).

accessibleName.description: Accessible name (e.g. aria-label) of the CTA element, when available.

cta_clicks.description: CTAs the engine actually clicked, one entry per click action executed. Distinct from finish_page_ctas, which records all visible CTAs on a page regardless of whether they were clicked.

timestamp.description: Final action-serialisation timestamp -- read once this record is built, well after dispatch/settling/the capture window close. See actionAnalytics.physicalClickDispatchedAt/captureWindowStartedAt/captureWindowEndedAt for the actual timeline.

sourcePageUrl.description: URL of the page the CTA was clicked on.

ctaText.description: Visible text of the clicked CTA element as rendered on the page.

accessibleName.description: Accessible name (e.g. aria-label) of the clicked CTA element, when available.

destinationUrl.description: Destination URL of the CTA, when available (e.g. an anchor's href) at click time.

resultingUrl.description: Page URL after the click action completed, when known.

resultingTitle.description: Page title read immediately after the click action completed, when the click succeeded.

navigationSucceeded.description: Whether the click resulted in the page actually navigating to a new URL.

actionSucceeded.description: Whether the click action itself executed without error.

error.description: Error message when the click action did not succeed.

actionAnalytics.description: Generic, action-attributed analytics evidence for this click, present only when captureModules also requested data_layer_evidence and/or ga4_network_events.
